# Temple Scroll Column 24 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 24 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 24:2 — "binding" vs. "restraining" vs. "tethering"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "binding" | Literal rendering of the Hebrew |
| LOGOS | "restraining" | Conveys the functional purpose |
| PNEUMA | "tethering" | Modern animal-handling vocabulary |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "restraining." More precise than EMET's "binding" for the function of holding animals in place for slaughter, without PNEUMA's informal register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:7 — "channel beneath the ground" vs. "subterranean conduit" vs. "underground drain"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "channel that is beneath the ground" | Literal descriptive phrase |
| LOGOS | "subterranean conduit" | Technical architectural vocabulary |
| PNEUMA | "underground drain" | Simple modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "subterranean conduit." Precise and appropriately formal for temple architecture.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:8 — "stranger" vs. "unauthorized person" vs. "layperson"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stranger" | Literal rendering of zar |
| LOGOS | "unauthorized person" | Clarifies the priestly-access restriction |
| PNEUMA | "layperson" | Modern term distinguishing clergy from laity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "unauthorized person." More precise than "stranger" (which implies ethnic exclusion) and more formal than "layperson" (which imports Christian ecclesiastical terminology).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:9 — "sprinkle" vs. "dash" vs. "throw"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sprinkle" | Common English for blood application |
| LOGOS | "dash" | Distinguishes zaraq (throwing) from hizzah (sprinkling) |
| PNEUMA | "throw" | Direct translation of zaraq |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "dash." This technical term correctly distinguishes the vigorous blood-throwing (zaraq) from the delicate sprinkling (hizzah) of purification rites.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:13 — "place" vs. "area" vs. "washing station"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "place" | Literal rendering of maqom |
| LOGOS | "area" | Slightly more specific |
| PNEUMA | "washing station" | Modern functional term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "place." The Hebrew maqom is deliberately general; "washing station" (PNEUMA) is anachronistically modern for a sacred text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 24:15 — "place of the ashes" vs. "ash-deposit" vs. "ash dump"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "place of the ashes" | Literal descriptive phrase |
| LOGOS | "ash-deposit" | Concise technical term |
| PNEUMA | "ash dump" | Modern informal equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "ash-deposit." Concise and appropriately dignified. "Ash dump" (PNEUMA) is too casual for sacred temple precincts.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
